---
title: "Setup"
---

Complete setup **before the first computational session**.

## Core requirements

- Git and a GitHub account when version control is part of the activity.
- Quarto for rendering course materials locally.
- A text editor or IDE appropriate to the language used in class.

## Computational environment

Only keep the sections that apply to the course.

### R

Record the required R version and packages. Use `renv` for courses where exact package versions matter.

### Python

Record the Python version and dependencies. Use `requirements.txt`, `environment.yml`, or another explicit environment specification.

### Julia

Record the Julia version and use `Project.toml` / `Manifest.toml` when reproducibility is required.

### C++ or compiled tools

Document compilers, system libraries, and platform-specific requirements.

## Verification

Give learners one minimal command or task that confirms their environment works before class.

## Data

Small teaching datasets may live in `data/`. Large, restricted, sensitive, or externally maintained data should be downloaded from an authoritative source instead of committed to Git.
